one_month_reasoning: I re-checked the EDGAR submissions feed on 1 Oct 2026. The latest filing is a director's Form 4 (deferred stock units) dated 30 Sep. There is no 8-K giving the Q3 results date. MP reported Q3 between 2 and 7 Nov in every year from 2021 to 2025, and MarketBeat lists 5 Nov 2026 as an unconfirmed estimate. I now put only about 10% on Q3 results landing before the 30 Oct close, down from 60-65% in round 1. That earlier figure came from a single TipRanks listing, which the supervisor rightly discounted. China's export-control suspension was extended at the 24-25 Sep summit to 10 Jan 2027, so that deadline also falls outside the window. That leaves no scheduled catalyst between 1 and 30 Oct. Following the brief, I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred just below spot (median $47.20, monthly sigma 0.20, which is close to 74%/3.5) and no longer widen it for earnings. Unscheduled risks are China rare-earth headlines and the 23% short interest, which fattens both tails. I see no momentum signal after the September slide from about $58 to the mid-$40s and the 6% rebound on 30 Sep.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods, all on about 239M fully diluted shares. (1) 20x EV/EBITDA on $430M of 2028E EBITDA, plus net cash, warrant proceeds and capped-call value, gives $41.0 (weight 0.5). (2) A pre-ramp sum of the parts gives $31.8 (weight 0.2). (3) Current 2028 consensus EBITDA of $540M at 18x, the multiple the market pays today, gives $45.7 (weight 0.3). This replaces round 1's stale CFRA run-rate method.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2028E adj. EBITDA $430M x 20x = EV $8.6B. Add net cash ex-converts at Sep-2027 of $0.55B, DoW warrant proceeds of $0.336B and capped-call value of $0.32B. Equity of $9.81B divided by 239M fully diluted shares = $41.0

inputs_detail.derivation: Built two ways. (a) 2028 consensus of $540M (MarketScreener) cut by about 20% for MP's record of slipping ramps; 2027 consensus has already fallen from $451.5M to $377.7M. (b) My own segment build of about $400M: Materials ~$230M, using Q2's $32.5M per quarter on 1,006 t (about 29% margin at the floor) scaled to about 6,000 t, plus some price above the floor; Independence ~$90M; 10X ~$40M as commissioning starts in 2028; heavy rare earths (HREE) ~$80M at ex-China Dy/Tb prices; corporate -$50M. I take a value between the two.

MP trades today at about 18x 2028 consensus EBITDA (EV of about $9.8B on 239M fully diluted shares, against $540M from MarketScreener). I apply 20x to a haircut base: the premium reflects the 10-year DoW floor and the 10X offtake (10-Q). This is down from 21x in round 1.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Materials $230M x 15x = $3.45B. Independence $90M x 15x = $1.35B. 10X net present value $1.0B. HREE $80M x 15x = $1.2B. Corporate -$50M x 12x = -$0.6B. Net cash plus warrant plus capped call $1.21B. Total about $7.6B / 239M = $31.8

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 Materials adjusted EBITDA was $32.5M on 1,006 t sold, including $17.6M of PPA income, so about $130M a year at 4,000 t. I scale to about 6,000 t with operating leverage and allow some price above the $110 floor. This is down from $300M in round 1, which assumed a 45% margin the reported segment data do not support.

$140M of escalating guaranteed EBITDA x 14x = $1.96B, less capex still to spend after Sep-2027 (more than $1.25B in total, offset by about $200M of incentives), discounted because commissioning only starts in 2028. This is down from $1.56B in round 1.

Dy/Tb separation starts in H2-2026 and a nine-figure Gd offtake has been signed. Ex-China Dy is about $3,500/kg and Tb about $6,745/kg (Benchmark Q3 2026). These multiples apply before the ramp has happened, so they sit below the market's 18x.

bear.story: NdPr stays under the $110 floor, so the PPA makes up most of the EBITDA. GM magnet shipments and the Independence ramp slip into late 2027, HREE yields disappoint, and 10X capex overruns or needs equity. Consensus 2028 EBITDA falls toward $350-400M. A durable US-China deal by 10 Jan 2027 removes the scarcity premium. The stock trades down to about the value of the floor, the 10X guarantee and net cash (about $22-28 a share).

base.story: Volumes reach 1,000-1,300 t a quarter with the floor binding. GM commercial magnet shipments begin in Q4-26 and ramp through 2027, and first Dy/Tb sales come at ex-China premiums. 2027 EBITDA lands near $300-380M with free cash flow still negative. The market keeps paying about 18-20x 2028 EBITDA of about $450M, so the stock ends slightly below today's price.

bull.story: The truce lapses on 10 Jan 2027 or China re-escalates on heavy rare earths, and NdPr rises above $130/kg. HREE sales scale at more than $3,000/kg Dy, Independence ships more than 1,000 t, and new defense or OEM offtakes are signed. The market looks through to EBITDA of $700M or more, and the stock re-rates toward the 2025 spike levels.

thesis_break_reason: Lowered from $30. Using the 10-Q, the contracted value (Materials at the $110 floor, about $1.0B net present value for the 10X guarantee, net cash, warrant proceeds and the capped call) comes to about $22-28 a share on 239M fully diluted shares, and my pre-ramp sum of the parts gives $31.8. A trade at $28 would mean the market is assigning roughly nothing to Independence magnets or heavy rare earths. That most likely points to a failed GM qualification, a 10X funding gap or equity raise, or a change in DoW support. It is about 1.4 quarterly sigmas (74% annual vol) below spot, which is more than ordinary noise over a few months, although not over a full year at 74% volatility.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results (estimated; MP has not announced a date and reported Q3 on 2-7 Nov in 2021-2025). Watch for production above 1,000 t, GM shipment timing, first Dy/Tb output, capex and any change in bill-and-hold.
First commercial NdFeB magnet shipments to GM from Independence (GM's remaining $45.5M prepayment is in current deferred revenue)

Extended expiry of China's suspension of its expanded rare-earth export controls (moved from 10 Nov at the 24-25 Sep 2026 summit). A lapse is a right-tail event; a durable deal is a left-tail event for the scarcity premium.
Q4/FY2026 results and the 2027 capex and volume outlook
2030 notes become cash-callable (if conditions are met). Forced conversion would add 34.4M shares, offset up to $31.06 by the capped call.
Apple recycled-magnet deliveries, no earlier than late 2027 per the 10-Q

key_uncertainties: Most of today's EBITDA is policy: PPA income was 62% of Q2 adjusted EBITDA. The NdPr price path relative to the $110 floor drives the upside.
Whether 2027-28 EBITDA can step up about 3x from the ~$114M run rate (2027 consensus is $377.7M and still being cut)
Execution on the Independence magnet ramp and GM qualification
HREE yields and how long ex-China Dy/Tb premiums last
10X capex (more than $1.25B) and funding, with cash down from $1.83B to $1.45B in H1-26 and a $500M minimum-cash covenant
What happens to China's export controls on 10 Jan 2027
reasoning: Round 2. I accept the supervisor's fact-checks and verified the two that matter most for my numbers in primary documents. (1) The Q2 10-Q capped-call note: it covers 34.4M shares from $21.74 to $31.06, worth about $0.32B above the cap, which I had left out. (2) The EDGAR submissions feed on 1 Oct: no 8-K setting a Q3 date, so the TipRanks 29 Oct date I relied on is unsupported, and MP's Q3 history points to about 5 Nov. I also take on board, citing the supervisor's sources: the truce extension to 10 Jan 2027 (CNBC 24 Sep), current consensus EBITDA of $377.7M for 2027 and $540M for 2028 (MarketScreener), and NdPr spot below the floor. The biggest correction to my own numbers came from rereading the Q2 segment data. Materials earned $32.5M on 1,006 t at the floor, a margin of about 29%, not the 45% I assumed. So my bottom-up 2028E falls to about $400M, close to a 20% haircut on the $540M consensus. I dropped the 2025 CFRA $850M x 23x method (25% weight) as stale and replaced it with a market-implied cross-check of 18x 2028 consensus. Fair value moves from $45.5 to $41.0 ($41.0 / $31.8 / $45.7 at weights 0.5 / 0.2 / 0.3). I end up below the supervisor's $44 because my own segment build supports less than consensus. I keep my view that the floor and DoW contracts support the low end and that the $74 sell-side mean is stale (targets are being cut: JPM to $60). For the 12-month ladder I don't expect the price to converge fully on fair value within a year. Policy optionality (the January cliff) and 23% short interest keep the right tail fat, so I set the median at $45, between fair value and spot, with sigma 0.60 below the median and 0.68 above. I trimmed the far-left tail slightly for the floor, $1.45B of cash and the DoW's $30.03 entry price. Mean is about $49 with roughly 30% below $33. Research in round 2 was limited to EDGAR and the 10-Q, plus the supervisor's cited pages.
